description:
Wir sind XO, eine Creator-Management-Agentur. Als Growth Manager übernimmst du die Short-Form-Strategie von 2-4 Creators von A bis Z: Scripts, Shot Lists, Feedback an Creator und Editoren, und ständiges Testen bis die Zahlen stimmen. Dein einziges echtes Ziel: Views, die zu echter Reichweite werden.
Aufgaben
Virale Short-Form-Videos analysieren, verstehen warum sie funktioniert haben, und das für unsere Creator adaptieren.
Scripts und Shot Lists schreiben, die deine Creator dann aufnehmen. Ihnen präzises Feedback geben, was gut war, was nicht, was sich ändern muss.
Editoren und Poster steuern. Du besitzt das Ergebnis, sie führen aus.
Jeden Post analysieren: warum hat das eingeschlagen, warum ist das gefloppt, worauf setzen wir diese Woche.
Mutige Ideen schnell testen, wegwerfen was nicht funktioniert, skalieren was funktioniert.
Qualifikation
Das ist kein 9-to-5. Wenn Sonntagabend ein Reel viral geht, bist du dran. Wenn unter der Woche um 22 Uhr ein Account gesperrt wird, kümmerst du dich. Das Wochenende ist normalerweise frei, aber bei Emergencies springst du ein, ohne Diskussion. Wenn dich das abschreckt, ist der Job nichts für dich.
Was wir wollen:
Besessenheit von Short-Form. Du schaust täglich stundenlang freiwillig TikTok und Reels und kannst erklären, warum ein Video funktioniert. Du lernst das nicht erst, du lebst es schon.
Ownership-Mentalität. Du behandelst die Accounts deiner Creator wie dein eigenes Business. Keine Ausreden, kein "der Editor hat nicht geliefert", du machst es möglich.
Analytischer Blick. Du kannst dir 20 Videos anschauen und uns sagen, welches Muster die erfolgreichen verbindet.
Fließend Deutsch und gutes Englisch. Nicht verhandelbar.
Bonus, kein Muss: Erfahrung im Aufbau von IG- oder TikTok-Accounts, Agentur- oder Marketing-Hintergrund. Uns zählt Drive und Gespür mehr als dein Lebenslauf.
Benefits
2.500 EUR Grundgehalt + leistungsbasierte Boni. Realistisch 3.000-6.000 EUR/Monat, je nach Ergebnissen.
100% remote. Arbeite von wo du willst.
Direkter Einfluss. Kleines Team, keine Bürokratie. Deine Ideen gehen diese Woche live, nicht nächstes Quartal.
Klarer Aufstieg. Wer wirklich pusht, kann in 8-12 Monaten Head of Marketing werden und ein eigenes Team führen.

description:

Collaborate with our contributor community and greater Documentation team to develop and improve documentation standards and processes.

You have 5-10 years experience researching and developing documentation for technical topics, like databases, APIs, cloud infrastructure, and performance and security monitoring.


You have 2-5 years experience managing a small team of technical writers, coaching their performance, guiding their career journey, and breaking down complex projects into achievable plans.


You have publicly available technical writing samples.


You are comfortable reading at least two programming languages (e.g. Ruby, Python, Go, bash).


You have written or managed documentation as code, and are familiar with modern infrastructure such as IaaS cloud services and containers, as well as Git/GitHub and CI/CD tooling.


You enjoy partnering with product managers, developers, and other SMEs to create robust technical documentation for developers and other types of users.

Self-starter capable of operating independently to drive meaningful business results

Proven experience to lead complex negotiations involving bespoke commercial agreements

Preferred Qualifications

5+ years of experience specifically selling fraud solutions for payments to enterprise customers

title: Client Services Representative
description:
The traditional financial industry was not built to put the interests of clients first. At Wealthfront, we’re committed to building products and services that are designed to earn our clients more and make it easy to bank, invest, and plan for the future. And we don’t want to stop there – our vision is to optimize our clients’ money across spending, savings, and investments, putting it all to work effortlessly. Deposit a paycheck with Wealthfront and, with the click of a button, our clients can have us automate the rest. Our software can top off emergency funds, pay all of our clients’ bills, and even invest the rest to help meet their goals. We call this future Self-Driving Money™.
 
Being a Client Services Representative at Wealthfront offers unique opportunities when compared to other roles that require a Series 7. The one that stands out most is that you would work for a company that actually intends to act in our clients' best financial interest and that treats clients the way we'd like to be treated. We always try to remove the traditional financial jargon and communicate with our clients in a clear and honest manner. By working at Wealthfront, you get to work at a company that doesn't require you to justify the unjustifiable, like high fees and actions that may not be in your best interest, because at Wealthfront, we put our clients' interests first.

About Wealthfront
 
Here at Wealthfront, our mission is to create a financial system that favors people, not institutions. We do this by leveraging technology to build powerful, low-cost, and easy-to-use financial products that help modern investors grow and manage their money.
 
We started with the ambition to transform the investment advisory business. By automating strategies typically reserved for the wealthy, we unlocked access to high quality investment advice for a digitally-native generation that was underserved by traditional institutions. Since then, we've expanded to a full suite of products designed to help our clients turn their savings into long-term wealth, including:
 
• A Cash Account that, through our partner banks, offers one of the highest annual percentage yields on uninvested cash in the industry, while providing instant and secure access to your money with no account fees and a full suite of checking features.
 
• A zero-commission Stock Investing Account with 50+ handpicked collections that help DIY investors discover new companies and make smarter investing decisions.
 
• Multiple automated investing portfolios designed to unlock tax savings through sophisticated strategies like fixed income, tax-loss harvesting, and direct indexing—which we offer at industry-leading low costs and accessible minimums.
 
Our award-winning products have attracted over 1 million clients who trust us with more than $100 billion of their hard earned savings—and we're far from done. If you’re inspired to help us reshape the financial industry as we create our next chapter, let’s talk!
 
For more information please visit www.wealthfront.com.We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
 
 
Please review our candidate privacy notice.

title: Senior Manager, Software Engineering - RL Post-Training Frameworks
description: Can you bring together globally distributed teams and the systems they build into a production-quality reinforcement learning ecosystem for researchers and model builders? Reinforcement learning post-training is where modern AI systems learn to reason, use tools, follow detailed instructions, and act as agents. Making that capability work at scale creates one of the most demanding systems problems in AI: a single RL run ties together inference, rollout, reward and critic evaluation, and training. At frontier scale, these loops have to run reliably across GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage, and open-source runtimes. You will lead the work to build, extend, and harden the rapidly evolving pieces to compose cleanly and scale with the most ambitious RL projects on NVIDIA's platforms.To meet that challenge, NVIDIA is building an RL Frameworks engineering team for the open-source tools and infrastructure that researchers, model builders, and external partners depend on. We are looking for a Senior Software Engineering Manager to set strategy, build the team, and convert emerging technical, customer, and partner signals into clear engineering priorities. The role spans RL frameworks such as VeRL, Miles, Slime, SkyRL, TorchTitan, and related post-training stacks, along with the systems those stacks build on and compose with: Megatron-Core, Ray, Monarch, NIXL, SGLang, Kubernetes, and NVIDIA platform libraries. Come build the ecosystem that the next generation of AI will rely on!What you will be doing:You will own NVIDIA's RL post-training frameworks strategy: where we invest directly, where we partner upstream, and how we prioritize based on customer impact, ecosystem leverage, technical feasibility, and opportunity cost. This is senior technical leadership work: using systems depth to evaluate architecture and performance claims across training, inference, rollout, orchestration, and the NVIDIA platform. You will help expert teams converge on integrations that improve RL framework quality and user value, then turn those decisions into measurable execution plans. The work includes benchmarking and reproducibility criteria, delivery across open-source frameworks and distributed runtimes, and close partnership with product management, research, DevRel, customer-facing teams, hardware, CUDA, networking, math libraries, compilers, and external open-source collaborators.You will also build the team: recruiting and developing managers and senior ICs, creating an effective US/APAC operating model, reviewing capacity against commitments, and setting clear ownership and decision rights. You will coach engineers to contribute credibly in open-source ecosystems and carry NVIDIA's priorities through high-quality upstream work. Because the technical work crosses organizations by design, you will turn open technical and partner questions into concrete and measurable action, set delivery goals, and hold the quality bar. Success means validated, valuable work rather than work that merely lands, plus durable open-source improvements that make RL workloads run well on NVIDIA systems.What we need to see:MS or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience)10+ years of software engineering experience in distributed systems, AI frameworks, ML infrastructure, high-performance computing, or systems software, with 4+ years as an engineering manager for software teamsStrong technical background in distributed AI systems, including the ability to reason across training, inference, orchestration, and end-to-end performance, and challenge architecture and performance tradeoffs with senior engineersExperience defining domain-level technical strategy, making build-vs-buy or upstream-vs-internal investment decisions, and creating multi-team execution plansAbility to drive engineering work across organizational boundaries, influence without direct authority, and communicate tradeoffs clearly to senior leaders and executivesEx

title: Why do you want this new job
description: No matter which side of the table youâve sat during interviews, youâve probably heard this question:  âWhy do you want this new job?â   In the recent past, Iâve interviewed a few candidates and heard the following answers so far:    Iâm not learning much on the current job after itâs been 2-4 years.  Iâm looking for something that offers better work-life balance.  Iâm not really looking for a job. The recruiters got in touch and I thought Iâd discuss.  Iâm looking for more challenging work.    All of the above are valid answers. I think thereâs another perfectly valid answer that candidates seldom mention probably due to the gravity of the interview room situation. Iâve interviewed over a hundred candidates across different companies and am yet to find anyone that mentions:  I am not happy with my current salary and benefits compared to my skills   Back to topic of answers. So, when someone answers that they are not learning new things on the job, obviously, youâd be curios to know why and how they have tried to change things. Unfortunately, most candidates simply mention that they are doing repeat work and thereâs not much to learn doing the same thing over and over again. This is where I start feeling a little uneasy. However, I understand that itâs a true statement. If youâre in a similar situation, hereâs some suggestion: read books, and write code based on what youâve read. Then, you can tell a much convincing story that, Iâve forced myself to learn new things and hereâs some proof, but I really want to apply the newly learned skills outside the scope of the âhello worldâ skills.  About work-life balance, I totally hear you. And if your current job doesnât suit what you need out of your life, itâs a perfectly valid reason to look for new opportunities. However, make sure youâre able to clearly set the expectation with your potential employer about what work-life balance means for you. For example, if you canât work over 40 hours a week, or must work from home one-two days a week, itâs best to discuss this even before an interview starts to ensure youâre a good match with the employer.  If you showed up at in interview just because a recruiter got in touch, Iâd say introspect first. Itâs possible that on our subconcious mind you have expectations that the potential of the new job offers you something that you donât get at the current job. So, instead of a passive asnwer that the you simply acted based on the recruiterâs invite, itâs much convincing to see if you can lay down one or two things that you expect from the new job that you donât get at the current job.  About looking for more challenge, it sounds like a cliche unless you can share examples of work that is of challenging to you. May be you like the challenge of using more complicated algorithms, may be you like dealing with a lot of data, may be you like supporting production emergencies, but thereâs gotta be something that you can explicitly mention as challenging. It helps employers to understand if theyâre able to provide you with enough challenge on the job.  Finally, if youâre looking for a new job because the current job isnât paying upto the level of your skills and contributions, make sure to communicate it clearly as well. With salaries and benefits, I find it much easier to work with people that know the actual $ figure thatâll make them happy instead of beating around the bush to create confusions all around. Just be confident and tell what makes you happy. If the employer can afford it, most likely theyâll want to get you onboard as a happy employee. If they canât afford it, theyâll do their best. The key here is to be explicit about what you want and be sure and confident about it.  In a nutshell, when you walk into an interview itâs yours to lose. The potential employer is investing their time and resources and would rather have you hired than having to interview

title: Design Engineer / UI
description:
Stark wachsendes Start-up:

6-Stelliges Gehalt 💰 + Bonus 🧨 + Anteile am Unternehmen 🏦

Du designst das Produkt.

Unser Mission

Jeder Mensch soll mit dem, was er weiß und kann, ein eigenes Einkommen aufbauen können.

Dafür haben wir die Finanz-Infrastruktur der Creator Economy in Europa gebaut. Produkte erstellen, Verkaufen, Bezahlen, Steuern, Auszahlung, Konto, Karte, Content hochladen. Alles, was zwischen einem Creator und seinem Geld steht, übernehmen wir.

Über BRYGHT laufen heute mehr als 50 Millionen Euro im Jahr, und wir sind erst am Anfang. Wir hören nicht auf, bevor jeder Creator in Europa über BRYGHT verdient.

Was BRYGHT ist

BRYGHT ist eine Plattform, kein Tool. Ein Creator baut hier seine Community, seine Kurse, seinen Shop und seinen Link in Bio. Seine Mitglieder kommen jeden Tag zurück, um zu lernen, zu chatten und zu kaufen. Wir kümmern uns um alles dahinter: Checkout, Zahlungen, Steuern, Auszahlungen.

Mobile first. Die meisten Mitglieder öffnen BRYGHT auf dem Handy, im Feed, im Chat, im Kurs. Creator arbeiten auf dem Desktop: Produkte anlegen, Community verwalten, Zahlen lesen. Beides muss sich anfühlen wie ein Produkt, das man gerne öffnet. Beides ist dein Spielfeld.

Die Rolle

Du bist die Person, wegen der BRYGHT sich anfühlt wie ein Produkt, das man liebt.

Heute funktioniert BRYGHT aber es ist noch nicht perfekt. Es ist noch nicht schnell genug. Es fühlt sich noch nicht an wie Linear, Stripe oder Instagram. Genau diese Lücke ist dein Job. Nicht Design oder Engineering. Beides. Du siehst, was falsch ist, und du bist derselbe Mensch, der es fixt.

Checkout, Feed, Kurs-Editor, Dashboards, Link in Bio, Nutzerprofil. Jeder Pixel, den ein Creator oder ein Käufer berührt, gehört dir.

Was du machst

  • Du baust BRYGHT neu auf. Von der Skizze bis Production. Das Produkt gehört dir.

  • Du besitzt unser Design System. Komponenten, Tokens, Motion. Am Ende sieht alles aus wie ein Produkt, nicht wie zehn.

  • Du nimmst einen Screen von unserem UX Lead und shippst ihn in Tagen, nicht in Wochen.

  • Du öffnest morgens BRYGHT, findest fünf Sachen, die dich stören, und bis abends sind drei davon weg. Niemand hat dich darum gebeten.

  • Du machst BRYGHT schnell. Ein langsames Interface ist ein schlechtes Interface.

Was du kannst

  • Du hast Interfaces gebaut, die echte Menschen jeden Tag benutzen. Du kannst sie uns zeigen.

  • Du schreibst Production-Frontend. Tailwind fließend, Hotwire oder React, und du findest dich in einer Rails-Codebase zurecht.

  • Du hast Geschmack. Du kannst zwei Screens nebeneinanderlegen und in einem Satz sagen, warum einer besser ist.

  • Typografie, Spacing, States, Motion, Ladeverhalten, Empty States, Fehler. Für dich sind das keine Details, das ist das Produkt.

  • Du prototypst im Code, nicht in Slides. Figma ist ein Werkzeug, kein Ort, an dem Dinge liegen bleiben.

  • Du arbeitest mit AI-Tools, als wären sie Teil deiner Hand. Cursor, Claude Code, Astra was auch immer dich schneller macht, bekommst du von uns.

  • Du weißt, warum sich Linear, Vercel und Stripe so anfühlen, wie sie sich anfühlen, weil du es auseinandergenommen hast.

Wie du arbeitest

Du bist cracked. Das heißt nicht, dass du 80 Stunden arbeitest. Das heißt, dass du nicht aufhören kannst, bevor es richtig ist.

Du brauchst keinen fertigen Spec. Du brauchst ein Problem und einen Zugang zur Codebase. Du shippst lieber Freitag etwas, das 80 Prozent gut ist, und machst es Montag zu 95, als drei Wochen auf Perfektion zu warten, die nie kommt. Du hast Meinungen, du vertrittst sie, und du gibst sie auf, wenn jemand ein besseres Argument hat. Du hast Nebenprojekte, die niemand bestellt hat, weil du einfach nicht anders kan

title: Developer Relations Engineer - UK
description:

Legendary brands like Virgin Media O2, Oatly, and TomTom use Storyblok to make a bigger, faster market impact.

You will be joining a growing company where you can contribute to many “firsts”. Plus these benefits:

Storyblok and headless CMS authority support and reduce onboarding friction with the developer community through code sample creation, debugging, direct partner engagement, and long-tail support channels. Monitor external communities on Discord, Twitter, LinkedIn, and Dev.to to identify new content to create.

  • Passionate and highly knowledgeable about advanced topics and latest trends around web development.
  • Demonstrates AI literacy, with the ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, decision-making, and quality of work while applying sound judgment and critical thinking.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • 5+ years of experience in web development.
  • Experience with CMS in general; experience with Headless CMS is a plus.
  • Thorough knowledge of consuming RESTful APIs. GraphQL API

title: Full-Stack Engineer
description:
A hedge fund analyst covering therapeutics has to watch hundreds of companies at once: press releases, SEC filings, management calls, updates on government sites, clinical data publications. Obi9 ingests all of it and surface what matters. Hedge funds pay for it today.
We are early and the team is small, so you would own entire surfaces of the product rather than pick up tickets:
- Ship full-stack features end to end, from the data model to the interface.
- Build the ingestion and enrichment pipelines that turn raw data into rich insights and alerts.
- Work on AI-backed features, from ideation to serving them in the webapp and over MCP.
- Make heavy data legible: dense tables, financial charts, document viewers, a live alert stream.
Stack: React + TypeScript, Node, Elixir, Python, distributed AI pipelines.
Beyond full-stack ability we want someone who already understands one of these worlds. One is enough, we are not asking for all four:
- Financial information systems. Bloomberg, FactSet, AlphaSense, Capital IQ, PitchBook. You know what entity resolution, identifier mapping and point-in-time data cost to get right.
- Financial domain knowledge in healthcare. Equity research, valuation, or time spent living inside filings and models.
- Audio and transcription. OtterAI Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Whisper. Diarization, speaker attribution, turning messy call audio into something quotable.
- AI-intensive products where the pipeline IS the product. Legal AI, document intelligence, medical coding. You know what evals, grounding and extraction schemas that hold actually cost.
Minimum: 5+ years building production web applications, a technical degree, fluency with current AI tooling, and eight continuous hours inside the 8:30am to 5:00pm ET window.
Apply: https://obi9.ai/jobs/full-stack-engineer?tab=apply

title: Data Analytics Partner, People Analytics
description:
Role Description

At Dropbox, people are our greatest asset. The People Analytics team partners closely with leaders across the company to help them make better, data-informed decisions about how we identify, attract, develop, and retain top talent. As Dropbox continues to scale and evolve its Talent Acquisition strategy, we’re looking for a Data Analyst who is passionate about problem-solving and using data to shape how we hire.

In this role, you’ll partner deeply with Talent Acquisition, People Partners, and business leaders to analyze hiring data, uncover trends, and surface insights that influence workforce planning, recruiting strategy, and candidate experience. You’ll work across quantitative and qualitative data to understand what drives successful hiring outcomes, where bottlenecks exist, and how we can improve efficiency, quality, and equity in our hiring processes.

You should have a demonstrated ability to think analytically about the business, translate ambiguous questions into structured analyses, and deliver clear, actionable insights. Success in this role requires strong attention to detail, high standards for data quality, and the ability to communicate findings in ways that drive real decisions.

Responsibilities

  • Partner on analytics initiatives to understand and improve the effectiveness, efficiency, and quality of hiring across Dropbox.
  • Create clarity from ambiguity, bringing structure to complex data and stakeholder narratives to identify the underlying question, establish analytical rigor, and drive actionable conclusions.
  • Monitor and analyze core Talent Acquisition metrics, proactively identifying trends and uncovering the “what” and “why” behind changes in performance.
  • Build strong relationships with key stakeholders; lead requirements gathering and translate business questions into clear analyses and insights that inform People and business leader decisions.
  • Answer complex business questions through independent investigation and data forensics, leveraging the data warehouse to deliver timely, high-impact insights.

About TestGorilla

At TestGorilla, we're on a mission to place 1 billion people in their dream jobs. To democratize opportunity, we're building the world's leading skills-based talent discovery platform - one that replaces reliance on resumes with scientific validation of what people can truly do.

Founded as a 100% remote company in 2020, our global team is united by high standards, a lot of heart, and a relentless drive to conquer new technological frontiers. We're all AI-fluent builders who care deeply about replacing bias with fairness.

After empowering thousands of companies to hire smarter and faster, we're now unlocking the next phase of our scale-up journey - where you'll play an instrumental role in creating a world where skills matter most!

About the role

As our Senior People & Talent Operations Partner, you'll own People Ops as a product: the systems, compliance, and self-serve workflows that let most of People & Culture run itself day to day, plus the tooling behind how we hire. You'll join a lean, two-person team, working directly with me, with proper and lasting ownership from day one. 

Payroll, compliance, and HR systems across every (35, currently!) country we operate in are foundational elements of this role. Just as critically, you'll build and own the AI/automation and self-serve layer that keeps our People function lean, bringing a product mindset to everything you touch.  Let’s face it: we’re a scale-up, so you’ll also need to be happy wearing other People hats when the moment requires.

We're looking for someone autonomous, opinionated and candid, who'll tell me when I've got it wrong. You'll be dealing with real people and real problems, so you'll need to stay empathic but boundaried, structured and organized even when the pace picks up.

I’m biased, but I think it’s a dream job: this is an HR role in an HRTech company changing the world of work for the better, we’ll have immense amounts of fun, there’s plenty of uncharted territory for you to make your own, and I’m committed to helping you to do the best work of your life.

A quick check: if you've never built objectively clever automations (not just used one someone else built), this probably isn't the role for you. Automation is just that central to the job.
